author: MsJasi
title: Save Your Money and Your Sanity
content:
I strongly discourage anyone from downloading Fishdom. This game is nothing like what is advertised. The ads make it look like you’re going to solve fun, interactive puzzles and actually have a meaningful impact on the aquarium. In reality, the gameplay quickly becomes repetitive and frustrating.

What’s even worse is how difficult the levels become. You can spend an absurd amount of time trying to pass a single level, and the game constantly pushes you toward spending money for extra moves, boosters, lives, and other advantages. I have spent far more money on this game than I ever intended to, simply trying to get through levels that feel deliberately designed to be unnecessarily difficult.

At this point, it has completely taken the fun out of the game. Instead of playing because I’m enjoying myself, I find myself frustrated and feeling like I have to spend money just to make progress.

A game should be entertaining—not something that continually pressures you to open your wallet.

Don’t be fooled by the ads. Save yourself the frustration and save your money. I wish I had never downloaded it.

author: Pouponseal
title: It’s all about money now
content:
From the Facebook Fishdom page. Player review. I have been playing this game for 8 years. In the beginning, it was fun, exciting, and genuinely enjoyable. But over those eight years, I have watched the game slowly decline. Recently, however, that decline has accelerated dramatically.

Adding 10 extra diamond cards to the collection and removing the three-day Deep Dive and Snail Race events are just two examples. For players who truly enjoy the game and play it well, it has become almost impossible to keep up. We are the players who create the competition, the excitement, and the motivation for others.

It is now almost impossible to complete team chests, and I won't even mention the team tournaments anymore. Soon, the only players left will be those who spend real money every month. But even they will eventually leave, because the competitive players who kept the game alive and made it exciting are the ones who are disappearing.

What will remain then? Avatar frames and badges will effectively become paid content. Tournaments and mini-games will either be impossible to complete or simply not worth playing.

If there is no meaningful goal, what is the point of spending several days tapping the screen just to beat a single level? There are many match-3 games that are much more enjoyable and rewarding.

Even in our usually very active team, we've seen a clear decline over the past week. A couple of players have already quit, while the others are staying mainly because of friendships we've built over many years. But sooner or later, they will leave too.

I'm waiting to see what July brings, hoping that something changes. If nothing does, I will delete the game without any regret.

I understand that developers need to make money. But in my opinion, they have become greedy, and their focus has shifted away from making the game enjoyable for loyal players.

author: cory carmichael
title: Greedy Devs
content: I been playing this game for years, almost up to level 10k. But now the devs have ratcheted the levels. They made the easy levels almost impossible to pass unless u use power ups and gems on them. It leaves many, experienced players even, stuck on easy levels for days. I get that free games need microtransactions, especially if they don’t have ads, but this is shameless. It feels like a betrayal to lean into manufactured difficulty so hard and to make the game almost unplayable.
